findings.explanation: The English moves dinner preparation back into the afternoon.

findings.highlight: My left arm moves even though it reacts slow
findings.evidenceJa: 反応が遅いものの左腕は動く
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s left arm moves, although its response is slow.
findings.explanation: The ungrammatical adverb use mars the precise statement of limited recovery.

findings.governingReading: Shirou plans fried kajiki, a billfish category not specified more narrowly here.
findings.explanation: The English selects swordfish without source support.

findings.governingReading: Two people deliver the elongated pre-meal greeting together.
findings.explanation: The English typography removes the simultaneous double voice.

findings.highlight: maybe she has no intention of spending time around Tohsaka
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂と顔を合わす気はないのかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Shirou speculates that Rider may not wish to meet Rin face to face because Rin could become an enemy.
findings.explanation: The English broadens a conjectured refusal to meet into avoiding time around Rin generally.

findings.governingReading: Shirou guesses Rider may be in either the earthen storehouse or the dojo.
findings.explanation: The English again changes the traditional earthen storehouse into a shed.

findings.highlight: Sakura’s good at Western food and you’re good at Japanese food
findings.evidenceJa: 桜は洋食で、士郎は和食派
findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether Sakura favors Western cooking while Shirou is of the Japanese-food school or preference.
findings.explanation: The English changes stylistic preference into separate areas of cooking competence.

findings.governingReading: The dish consists of golden-fried cuts or fillets of kajiki.
findings.explanation: The English removes the concrete cut of fish and leaves a vague pronoun.

findings.governingReading: Illya happily eats potatoes explicitly simmered sweet.
findings.explanation: The English removes their sweetness, weakening the setup for Sakura’s contradictory report.

findings.highlight: I-I made such a stupid mistake
findings.evidenceJa: そんなたわけたミスを……！？
findings.governingReading: Before tasting the dish, Shirou reacts in disbelief at the possibility of making such an absurd mistake in a familiar recipe.
findings.explanation: The English converts his alarmed, unfinished question into an admission that the mistake occurred.

findings.governingReading: Shirou finds the seasoning is properly the same as he always makes it.
findings.explanation: The English loses the comparison to his established recipe and says only that it tastes normal.

findings.highlight: there’s something in it to bring out the flavor
findings.evidenceJa: 隠し味らしきものが入ってる
findings.governingReading: Rin detects what seems to be some kind of hidden or secret flavoring ingredient.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the ingredient a flavor-enhancing function that the source does not identify.

findings.governingReading: Illya says the sweetness is just right and makes the dish easy to eat.
findings.explanation: The English removes the calibrated appropriateness of the sweetness.

findings.evidenceJa: 肉じゃがに箸を伸ばす
findings.governingReading: Still unconvinced, Sakura extends her chopsticks toward the nikujaga to test it again.
findings.explanation: The English invents a second helping before the measured one-two-three-bite examination.

findings.governingReading: Sakura suggests she must have selected a lightly seasoned portion.
findings.explanation: The English changes weak seasoning into a piece that was not simmered at all.

findings.governingReading: After pausing to investigate and explain the discrepancy, Sakura resumes her meal.
findings.explanation: The English erases the interruption and restart.

findings.evidenceJa: とんでもなく元気だった
findings.governingReading: Sakura is extraordinarily energetic afterward despite Shirou’s unease.
findings.explanation: The English drastically weakens the conspicuous vigor into minimal adequacy.

findings.evidenceJa: 美味しそうに箸を進め
findings.governingReading: Sakura continues eating with apparent enjoyment while Rin watches in surprise.
findings.explanation: The English removes the appearance that the food tastes delicious to her.

findings.evidenceJa: おかずと米を片付けてくれた
findings.governingReading: Sakura completely finishes both the side dishes and the rice.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the two categories into undifferentiated food.
